claims.text: Composition variations modify local lattice distortion in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived FCC alloys.
Composition variations modify stacking fault energy in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived FCC alloys.
Local lattice distortion and stacking fault energy alter the balance between dislocation glide and twinning-mediated plasticity.
The balance between dislocation glide and twinning-mediated plasticity governs the mechanical-property differences among the alloys.
The investigated quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys can be prepared as single-phase FCC microstructures using identical thermomechanical treatments.
Keeping processing conditions constant isolates constituent selection as the intervention.
Identical thermomechanical processing and standardized testing ensure that mechanical differences arise solely from composition.
Local lattice distortions mediate dislocation motion.
Stacking fault energy mediates twin formation.
Increased lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and thereby strengthens the alloy.
Reduced stacking fault energy increases the propensity for deformation twinning.
Subsets with enhanced lattice distortion and reduced stacking fault energy will have greater yield strength and hardness than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Subsets with enhanced lattice distortion and reduced stacking fault energy may have lower or otherwise altered ductility relative to the baseline.
Compositions with reduced lattice distortion or higher stacking fault energy may have lower strength and different ductility profiles.
The proposed mechanism is limited to single-phase FCC alloys derived from Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni under controlled thermomechanical conditions.
Secondary phases, abnormal grain sizes, or substantially different processing histories may invalidate the proposed relationship.
Diffraction line broadening can provide a quantitative estimate of local lattice distortion.
TEM can characterize twin density and dislocation structures relevant to the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The conditions claim that identical processing ensures differences arise solely from composition, whereas the uncertainty statement acknowledges that slight microstructural differences may influence ductility. Identical nominal processing does not itself establish identical microstructures.
